title: Pedagogic Workshop Lays Foundation for Digital Teaching at GHS Mbonjo
body:
**Date:** 14 January 2026 · **Category:** Uncategorized · **Author:** admin

On Wednesday, 14 January 2025, staff of Government High School Mbonjo met in the staff room for a pedagogic workshop that began at 12 noon and ended at 2 pm. The session opened with a prayer, committing the work of the school and the success of its learners into God's hands. A group photograph was taken at the end of the workshop to mark the occasion.

The workshop focused on the strengthening of teaching through digital tools and proper academic monitoring. The key message of the day was delivered by the Regional Delegate for the South West Region, Buea, and presented to staff by the Principal. Special emphasis was placed on the correct filling of teachers' logbooks as a professional duty that ensures accountability and continuity of learning.

Staff were introduced to the **Digital Logbook System**, a new method of recording lessons that will come into use very soon. The Ministry of Secondary Education in Yaounde will monitor this system directly once it goes live. For now, teachers will continue with the paper logbook, but they were told to be ready for the immediate transition when the digital platform is activated. The new system will allow closer follow up of lesson delivery and greater accountability across all schools.

Although teaching materials are not yet on the school website, teachers were informed that all departments must submit their lesson notes, assignments, and other resources through the Computer Science Department. These materials will then be uploaded so that students can access them using their parents' phones while at home or during holidays.

To support digital teaching, free time has been allocated for teachers to use the Multimedia Laboratory for the preparation and delivery of online lessons. There was also a live demonstration of the digital board recently provided by the Minister of Secondary Education. Teachers were shown how it can be used to present lessons, write on the screen, and save content for future use.

The administration also presented the staff appointed to supervise and guide digital learning in the school:

| Role | Officer |
|---|---|
| Coordinator | Mrs. Jeff Bertha, Vice Principal |
| Technical Supervision | Mr. Ngwana Joshua |
| Counselling | Mrs. Enow Bisong Njonje |
| Discipline | Mr. Walters |

These officers will ensure that digital lessons are well planned, properly delivered, and that students remain focused and supported.

A session was also devoted to student evaluation. Teachers were guided on the best ways to assess learners in digital lessons, with emphasis on fairness, clarity, and encouragement. Staff were reminded that every student must be treated with dignity and that the guidance and counselling unit is always available to support learners facing difficulties.

The workshop closed with a shared sense of purpose. With the introduction of digital tools, direct monitoring by the Ministry, and a clear support structure within the school, GHS Mbonjo is now better positioned to deliver quality education that reaches students both in school and at home.

> ⚠️ **Note:** the post is dated January 2026 but the opening line says "Wednesday, 14 January 2025." One of the two years is wrong — worth fixing.

title: GHS Mbonjo Limbe Launches 2025 Club Activities
body:
**Date:** 3 December 2025 · **Category:** Activities · **Author:** admin

GHS Mbonjo Limbe held its official launch of club activities during a school assembly marked by strong participation and a warm spirit of community. The Principal, Mr David Moki, opened the event with words of appreciation to the teaching staff, students and the 2016 batch of ex-students who honoured the invitation. He noted that the involvement of former learners shows the lasting bond they share with the school.

During his remarks, the Principal awarded **Form 2B** for maintaining the cleanest classroom this term. He encouraged other classes to improve their hygiene and aim for the next award. As part of this effort, the 2026 batch of ex-students donated cleaning cans to support a "Clean School Campaign," reinforcing the school's commitment to a healthy learning environment.

The event was coordinated by **Madam Angu Grace**. Under her guidance, all registered clubs were presented to the student body. Each club introduced its aims and activities to help students make informed choices before official registration on **Wednesday 10 December**.

The student representative also addressed the assembly and highlighted the value of joining a club. He spoke especially on the opportunities offered by the Environmental Science Club and encouraged learners to take part in activities that improve their surroundings.

The event closed with a short address from the Principal. He thanked the organisers, teachers, club coordinators and students for their cooperation. He wished all learners a safe journey home and encouraged them to reflect on the clubs they may want to join.

title: 📢 Attention Parents, Students & Educators! The Official 2025-2026 School Calendar for Cameroon is HERE!
body:
**Date:** 19 August 2025 · **Category:** Uncategorized · **Author:** admin

At **GHS Mbonjo – A Dream Come True**, we believe that preparation is the key to success. The wait is finally over! The **Ministry of Basic Education (MINEDUB)** and the **Ministry of Secondary Education (MINESEC)** have officially released the **2025-2026 Cameroon School Calendar**.

### 🏫 The Big Picture: Start and End Dates
- **School Year Begins:** Monday, September 8, 2025, at 7:30 AM
- **School Year Ends:** Friday, July 31, 2026, at 3:30 PM

### ✈️ 2025-2026 School Holiday Breaks
- **Christmas/New Year Break:** Friday, December 19, 2025 (3:30 PM) → Monday, January 5, 2026 (7:30 AM)
- **Easter Break:** Thursday, April 2, 2026 (3:30 PM) → Monday, April 20, 2026 (7:30 AM)

### 📝 Major Examination Periods
- **Basic Education Exams:** May 11 – July 31, 2026
- **Secondary Education Exams:** May 13 – July 31, 2026
- **Épreuve Zéro (Mock Exams):** April 23–24, 2026
- **Practical PE Exams:** April 27 – May 15, 2026

### 🎉 Special Days & Weeks to Celebrate
- International Literacy Day → Sept 8, 2025
- World Teachers' Day → Oct 5, 2025 (celebrated in schools on Oct 6)
- National Week of Bilingualism → Jan 26 – 30, 2026
- Youth Week → Feb 3 – 11, 2026
- National Day of Arts & Culture → Mar 6, 2026
- "La Francophonie" Day → Mar 20, 2026
- **FENASSCO Games (Leagues A & B):** Held during the 2nd Term Break

### 👶 For Nursery & Pre-School Learners
Nursery pupils will enjoy **3 extra days of vacation** compared to primary and secondary students during each break. Schools are also encouraged to organize festive closing ceremonies for little learners.

### 🧠 Key Changes & Highlights
- **Flexible Learning:** A blend of in-person and distance learning (internet, TV, radio, booklets).
- **Remediation Time:** Built-in periods for students to catch up after evaluations.
- **Class Size Limits:** Nursery → 30 pupils/class · Primary → 60 pupils/class · Secondary → 50 students/class
- **900-Hour Minimum:** Regardless of disruptions, each school must deliver at least 900 teaching hours.

### 🧑‍🏫 For Teachers & Administrators
- **Pedagogic Days:** Sept 15 – Oct 13, 2025
- **UNAPED/UNIMAT Meetings:** Every 6 weeks
- **Staff Meetings:** Last Friday before 1st term + First Friday of 2nd & 3rd terms
- **Staff Holidays:** Begin July 31, 2026

### 📅 Term Overview
- **First Term:** Sept 8 – Nov 28, 2025
- **Second Term:** Dec 1 – Dec 19, 2025 & Jan 5 – Mar 6, 2026
- **Third Term:** Mar 9 – Apr 2, 2026 & Apr 20 – Jun 13, 2026
- **Holidays for non-exam classes:** Begin June 12, 2026

### 🌟 Final Word
At **GHS Mbonjo**, we are committed to helping students, parents, and teachers stay informed and prepared. This calendar provides the roadmap for a well-structured, impactful, and successful academic year.

✨ Together, let's make the **2025-2026 school year** another milestone in our journey of excellence.

🔖 *Tag: GHS Mbonjo – A Dream Come True*
📢 Don't forget to share this post with parents, students, and educators in your network!

`#CameroonEducation #BackToSchoolCMR #MINEDUB #MINESEC #SchoolCalendar2026`

title: Minister Nalova Lyonga Launches Distance Learning Pilot Centre in Limbe
body:
**Date:** 30 October 2024 · **Category:** Official Visits · **Author:** admin

The **Minister of Secondary Education, Professor Nalova Lyonga**, officially launched a **pilot distance learning centre** in Limbe to serve **Government Technical High School (GTHS) Bimbia** and **Government High School (GHS) Mbonjo**, both located in the Fako Division, South West Region.

The inauguration took place on **Friday, October 11**, at the shared school complex, and featured a live demonstration showcasing how students can benefit from remote learning technologies. The initiative, supported and equipped by **IHS Cameroon S.A.**, marks a significant step toward integrating digital learning into secondary education in Cameroon.

### The newly inaugurated ICT Centre includes:
- **30 desktop computers** (accommodating up to **60 students per session**)
- Comfortable seating
- High-speed internet access
- A projector
- A **solar backup system** to ensure consistent operation during power outages

During the ceremony, Minister Nalova Lyonga highlighted the government's vision to bridge the educational gap across regions by making quality teaching accessible nationwide, regardless of location. She emphasized the importance of discipline, dedication, and self-confidence among students, encouraging them to seize the opportunity offered through this innovation.

> "Students should believe in themselves, stay focused, respect school authorities, and work hard to succeed in their studies," she said.

The minister further explained that the purpose of distance learning is to modernize secondary education by enhancing **digital literacy and connectivity** in schools across the country. She noted that the government plans to renovate IT centres in various schools as part of the nationwide rollout of the distance education initiative.

After observing a sample lesson delivered live from Yaoundé, Minister Nalova praised the effectiveness of the system, which enables real-time interaction between teachers and students.

> "The demonstration showed that knowledge can be transmitted instantly from Yaoundé, with students actively engaging and teachers providing immediate feedback. It's like having a magical board," she remarked.

She reaffirmed the commitment of the Ministry of Secondary Education to ensure that every school—urban or rural—is equipped with modern digital tools, allowing all students equal access to quality education and instruction from the country's best teachers.

This innovative step reflects Cameroon's dedication to embracing technology in education and ensuring that no learner is left behind.

title: GHS Mbonjo Officially Opens the 2024/2025 Academic Year with a Warm Call to Serve and Embrace Digital Learning
body:
**Date:** 6 September 2024 · **Category:** Activities · **Author:** admin

On **Friday, September 6th, 2024**, at exactly 10:00 AM, the staff of Government High School (GHS) Mbonjo Limbe convened in the school's staff room for the official launching of the 2024/2025 academic year. The meeting marked not only the beginning of a new school year but also a moment of reflection, gratitude, and renewed commitment to the school's mission of excellence.

A key highlight of the event was the **retirement of the school's bursar**, a respected and longstanding member of the GHS Mbonjo family. In his farewell remarks, the outgoing bursar expressed heartfelt gratitude for the love and support he enjoyed throughout his years of service at the school.

> "I am always available to put in my service when needed," he said warmly, emphasizing his continued willingness to support the school community in any way possible.

He thanked the staff for the camaraderie and respect that made his time at GHS Mbonjo truly memorable. *(Mr. Anjua, the former GHS Mbonjo Bursar.)*

The meeting was presided over by the Principal, **Mr. David Moki Ndive**, who used the opportunity to officially welcome all staff back for the new academic year. In his address, the Principal emphasized the importance of teaching with **love, empathy, and a strong sense of parental responsibility** towards the students.

> "Let us teach in love for the students and act as their parents. Every student deserves care, guidance, and respect."

Mr. Ndive also reminded staff of the national educational vision led by the Minister of Secondary Education, calling on all teachers to **embrace digital learning** fully. He encouraged teachers to integrate technology into their classrooms and use modern tools to improve teaching and learning outcomes.

> "It is the Minister's goal that we should fully engage in digital learning. Let us not be left behind."

The tone of the meeting was one of unity, motivation, and professionalism as staff members pledged their commitment to a successful school year. With the right spirit and digital vision, GHS Mbonjo is poised to make significant strides in 2024/2025.

The academic year may have just begun, but the fire of purpose has already been lit in the hearts of those entrusted with shaping the next generation.

title: GHS Mbonjo Limbe Prepares to Host Athletes for 2024 FENASSCO A Finals
body:
**Date:** 14 February 2024 · **Category:** Official Visits · **Author:** admin

As the **2024 FENASSCO A National Finals** draw near, **Government High School (GHS) Mbonjo Limbe** is proud to be one of the official accommodation centres for athletes participating in this prestigious inter-school sports competition. The school has been diligently preparing its facilities and logistics to provide a safe, clean, and welcoming environment for the young athletes coming from various regions of Cameroon.

In recognition of the school's vital role in the event, the **Honourable Minister of Secondary Education, Professor Nalova Lyonga**, paid a special visit to the campus to assess the level of preparedness and to encourage staff and students. The minister's visit was marked by warmth, enthusiasm, and strong words of encouragement, as she inspected the dormitory spaces, hygiene facilities, classrooms, and general environment set aside for the athletes' stay.

During the visit, the Minister commended the administration of GHS Mbonjo for their commitment to excellence and community spirit. She urged the school to continue upholding high standards of hospitality, discipline, and cleanliness during and beyond the games.

> "It is not just about winning medals, but also about learning, building friendships, and creating a supportive environment where our young athletes can thrive," the minister remarked.

### As part of the preparations:
- Dormitories and classrooms have been cleaned and arranged to ensure comfort.
- Sanitary facilities have been refurbished to meet health and safety standards.
- School security has been reinforced to ensure a peaceful and organized environment.
- Staff and volunteers have been briefed and trained to assist with logistics and welfare.

The students and teachers of GHS Mbonjo have embraced this national duty with excitement and a strong sense of responsibility. It is a moment of pride for the entire school community to be part of a major event that celebrates youth talent, sportsmanship, and national unity.

The FENASSCO A Finals serve as a platform to not only identify sporting talent but also to promote discipline, team spirit, and educational values among students across Cameroon.

As the games approach, GHS Mbonjo Limbe stands ready—**not just as a host, but as a home away from home** for the nation's budding champions.
